clue.text: Oriental jeans ape ruined

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked and broken up, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: An Eastern pair of denims has been wrecked by a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan lies in the Far East, so anything from that nation counts as Oriental in the older sense of Eastern.

clue.text: First person in France with lady who is unsophisticated

parts.note: je is French for I
June is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone says 'I' in France beside a naive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: First person means the pronoun I, not the first person to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune can mean naive or simplistic, so it is a synonym for lacking worldliness.

clue.text: Volcanic rock turning up small animals

indicators.note: turning round sends the following word back to front

parts.note: taken as written
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: Lava stone is being overturned to reveal little creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous stone formed when frothy lava cools, so it is a kind of igneous rock.

clue.text: Senor struggling with strong headwind

indicators.note: a struggling thing writhes about, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the five letters of this Spanish title

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman battles against a fierce wind in his face.
explanation.definitionFit: A noser is a sailors' and dialect term for a strong wind blowing straight into one's face or bows.

clue.text: Rock music

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway back and forth
second meaning: a jazz style of the big-band era

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue looks like the music genre rock; separated, rock is the verb for moving to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway rhythmically is one sense, and the other is the 1930s and 1940s big-band jazz style of Benny Goodman.

clue.text: Flame coming from aeroplane on American fuel?

definitions.text: Flame coming from aeroplane on American fuel?

parts.words: Flame coming from aeroplane on American fuel?
parts.note: surface reading: fire streaming out of a plane that runs on US petrol
setter's reading: a type of jet engine whose burning exhaust thrusts an aircraft along, air being rammed in by forward speed

explanation.surface: Fire bursts from a plane running on fuel bought in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the clue is a playful description rather than a strict definition of a simple engine with no moving compressor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet burns fuel in air forced in by the craft's own speed, so a flame shoots out behind the plane.

clue.text: A rare mist dispersed by the wind

indicators.note: something dispersed is scattered about, so these letters are spread and gathered again in a new order

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: An unusual fog was blown away by a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Any current of moving air is wind, so the compound is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hector we will include as shopkeeper

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hector is to bully or taunt, to jeer
we will contracts to we'll

explanation.surface: We'll put up with a bullying trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a retailer selling rings and watches, so he is one particular kind of trader.

clue.text: Type it, I'd ingredients creating slight warmness

indicators.note: the words are used as raw materials, mixed together to produce something new

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Some typed words are the raw material for something lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid means lukewarm, so the abstract noun names a state of mild warmth.

clue.text: One-piece athletic wear?

parts.note: surface reading: a single garment worn by a sprinter or gymnast
setter's reading: the garment's name sounds like an event in athletics, the leaping one, plus a word for a set of clothes

explanation.surface: A single garment made for an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the garment is not really sportswear; its name merely contains a field event.
explanation.definitionFit: This all-in-one overall covers torso and legs together, originally worn by parachutists, so it is genuinely a one-piece garment.

clue.text: Mature wealthy leader found in the bunch

indicators.note: to be found in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bunch of people or things is a group

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

parts.note: the first letter of wealthy

explanation.surface: A grown-up rich head of the gang has been located among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The W sits after the first three letters of GROUP, giving GRO-W-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to mature is to become adult, which is exactly what this two-word phrasal verb means.

clue.text: Stuck in the traffic?

parts.note: surface reading: delayed in a queue of cars
setter's reading: wedged fast, unable to move, as in a congestion of vehicles

explanation.walkthrough: The word for blocked vehicles also means wedged fast in general, as a door or a jar lid can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A road choked with cars is a traffic jam, and anything fixed immovably in place is said to be thus stuck.

clue.text: Again cur struggled annexing a country!

indicators.note: to annex is to attach an extra part, so a further piece is joined on at the end
something that has struggled has thrashed about, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a different order

parts.note: the letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog fought once more to seize a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a republic in Central America, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: I'd let out that the roof was covered

indicators.note: letting letters out frees them from their order, so they can be set down differently

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits they revealed that the roof had been finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: saying the roof was covered is to say it was tiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs are commonly covered with slates or ceramic tiles, so a covered roof is a tiled one.

clue.text: Streams before noon washed up on the shore

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one in the answer

parts.note: jets are fast streams of liquid or gas
the hours before noon are a.m.

explanation.surface: Morning currents carried things in to the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard that later drifts in, the material washed up on the shore.

clue.text: Pal needs a new front

indicators.note: a new version means a fresh arrangement of the same letters

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A friend requires a fresh facade or show of confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Front here is the seafront, the promenade along a beach in a British resort town.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level walkway by the sea, which is what the British call the front.

clue.text: Savoury snack from Greek island before midday

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one in the answer

parts.note: Samos is an Aegean island
a.m. is before midday; here only its A

explanation.surface: A tasty bite brought from a Greek isle ahead of lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Before midday gives A, a short form of a.m.; the island Samos lies off Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry triangle filled with spiced vegetables or meat, a popular savoury nibble.

clue.text: Forcibly discharge from aeroplane perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw out or expel
second meaning: what a pilot does via an ejector seat, leaving the aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone is hurled out of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to expel by force, and is also the specific term for a pilot leaving a jet by ejector seat.

clue.text: Coated shortly?

parts.note: surface reading: given a coating in a moment
setter's reading: dressed in a short coat, a garment worn to the hips

explanation.walkthrough: Shortly seems to mean soon, but it describes the coat: a short coat goes by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes or people wearing an outer layer are jacketed, a jacket being a short coat.

clue.text: Deadlock for rugby player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an impasse where neither side gives way

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the stand-off is the fly-half, who links the scrum-half with the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse between two parties is a stalemate, and the British name for the rugby fly-half shares the term.

clue.text: How one caught out of bed will behave badly

parts.words: How one caught out of bed will
parts.note: surface reading: someone found out of bed is still awake and on their feet
setter's reading: to misbehave, as a naughty child does

explanation.surface: A child discovered out of bed after lights-out starts misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of bed suggests the second word, being up and about; read together the phrase means to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to misbehave or play up, as a child or a faulty machine does.

clue.text: Form of address used by first man interrupting me

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written; the outer piece
Adam is the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: The first man breaks in on someone using a polite title.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French courtesy title for a woman, a polite way of speaking to her.

clue.text: After almost 30 days, I take alternative being of lower rank

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
the single letter takes or adds on the next word, so the two are joined

parts.note: June has thirty days
taken as written
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: After nearly a month, I opt for another path as the lesser party.
explanation.walkthrough: June is the month of 30 days, so 'almost 30 days' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior is someone subordinate in standing or position, so the word fits a description of inferior status.

clue.text: Said to be every seven days but not in a strong way

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want a word that sounds the same as the one described

parts.note: occurring once each seven days

explanation.surface: A regular seven-day event apparently lacks strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something feebly, without force, which is how things are done not in a strong way.

clue.text: Some had taken Yaoundé to be the capital of this African country

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within a stretch of the clue

parts.note: found running across the end of one word and the start of the next
surface padding: the false claim about the seat of government gives no letters

explanation.surface: Some people wrongly believed Yaoundé was the capital of a certain African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Yaoundé is really the capital of Cameroon; the country sits hidden across 'taken Yaoundé'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African republic, whose real capital is Nairobi.

clue.text: Nominal subscription?

parts.note: surface reading: a token fee to join a club or take a magazine
setter's reading: one's name written beneath a document, sub-scribed being literally written under

explanation.walkthrough: Subscription looks like a membership fee and nominal like 'small'; read literally, it is the name written underneath a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing your name at the foot of a document is the literal sense of subscribing, hence the mark is a name written below.

clue.text: On hand it is fitting

parts.note: surface reading: it is appropriate that something is readily available
setter's reading: worn over the palm and fingers, shaped to fit them snugly

explanation.walkthrough: On hand normally means available; literally it is something sitting on the hand, and fitting means it fits snugly.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering for the fingers and palm is worn on the hand and must fit it, so the description matches.

clue.text: A retrogressive attitude for a moralist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retrogressive means moving backwards, so the following word is read back to front

parts.note: an attitude can mean a bodily stance, a pose

explanation.surface: A backward-looking outlook befits someone who preaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the Greek teller of fables, each ending with a moral, so he was a famous moralist.

clue.text: Strong hard-working person, one from an ancient city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who works like a ...; tireless and sturdy
second meaning: a citizen of Troy

explanation.surface: A tireless labourer comes from a city of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like this is an idiom for hard, determined labour, and the word also names a native of ancient Troy.

clue.text: It's a delight to remain with the aircraft column

parts.note: joy is delight
to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: It is a pleasure to stay beside the plane's control.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'It's a' is padding that lets the wordplay read as a sentence; 'column' is the upright control lever, not a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's joystick is the control lever, a short upright column used to steer an aircraft.

clue.text: Pudding about to be returned to useless old fellow

parts.note: duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff

indicators.note: to be returned is to be sent back the way it came, so the word about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A dessert is about to be sent back to an incompetent old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent or ineffectual person, often an older man; useless fellow is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pedro and Jay moved into great danger

indicators.note: the letters are moved around and turned into something else

parts.note: the letters of the two names

explanation.surface: Two men, Pedro and Jay, relocated into a perilous situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joins the two names in the fodder only; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in jeopardy is to be at risk of loss or harm, so the word is a synonym for serious peril.
